prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — I don’t know your case details yet, so I can’t pick a single lawyer for you. But I can tell you how to find the right Pleasanton-area car‑accident / personal‑injury attorney, what to ask at a consultation, what to watch out for, and — if you want — I can search and give a short list of local lawyers with contact info and ratings.

Quick questions so I can tailor recommendations:
- When did the crash happen?
- Are you still getting medical treatment? How serious are your injuries?
- Were you the driver, passenger, pedestrian, cyclist?
- Has the other driver’s insurance contacted you or made an offer?
- Do you already have an attorney or insurance company representing you?
- Any language preferences or other constraints (budget, willingness to go to trial)?

How to choose the right lawyer
1. Look for a specialist in car-accident / personal injury cases (not a generalist).
2. Prefer contingency-fee firms (they get paid only if you recover money).
3. Experience: ask about similar cases, settlements and trial experience.
4. Local knowledge: familiarity with Alameda County courts, local hospitals, and common insurance companies helps.
5. Resources: ability to hire medical experts, accident reconstruction, and investigators when needed.
6. Communication: timely responses and a point of contact (attorney or paralegal).
7. Reputation: client reviews, peer ratings, and disciplinary history via the California State Bar.

Where to verify and search
- California State Bar lawyer search (to confirm license and disciplinary record).
- Online review sites: Google Reviews, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Yelp.
- Local referrals: friends/family or the Alameda County Bar Association.

What to bring to the first (usually free) consultation
- Police report number or copy
- Photographs of the scene, vehicles, and injuries
- Medical records and bills (or at least dates and providers)
- Insurance information (yours and other driver’s)
- Any correspondence from insurance companies
- Names and contact info for witnesses
- Notes about how the crash happened

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled?
- Do you try cases or settle most claims? Trial experience?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your contingency fee and are there any other costs I might owe?
- How do you advance case costs (medical liens, expert fees)?
- What is a realistic range of outcomes for my case?
- How long will my case likely take?
- How will you communicate case status to me?

Typical fee and cost issues (CA)
- Contingency fees commonly range ~33% for pre‑lawsuit settlements, and up to 40%+ if a lawsuit and trial are required (percentages vary; read the fee agreement).
- You may still be responsible for out‑of‑pocket costs if you lose, depending on the fee agreement.
- Medical liens and health insurance subrogation can reduce net recovery — ask about handling of liens.

Red flags
- Attorneys who pressure you to sign immediately or guarantee a specific recovery amount.
- Poor or evasive answers about experience or whether they’ll try your case.
- No clear written fee agreement or unwillingness to put fee terms in writing.
- Very low price promises without explanation.

If you’d like, I can:
- Search for and provide a short list (3–5) of personal‑injury lawyers who handle car-accident cases in Pleasanton/Dublin/Livermore with contact info and ratings.
- Draft an email or call script you can use to contact attorneys and set up consultations.
Tell me which you prefer and answer any of the quick questions above so I can give tailored options.
